title: Silver Lime: Ancient Silver Limes You Can Visit
meta_description: A lime whose leaves flicker silver in the wind, mapped in a castle park, a former private garden and a Dutch town that may take its own name from the tree.
intro: Silver lime carries its identifying trick on the underside of every leaf: a coat of fine white felt that flickers the whole crown between green and silver on a windy day, readable from thirty metres away. It is the last lime to flower, in July. Tilburg's oldest tree, standing off the main square where nobody thinks to look, grows in a town that may take its own name from the species. A second Tilburg lime, in a small park on the Fokkerpad, stood in a private garden laid out by Leonard Springer before the estate opened to the public. Bruges planted three at the Gentpoort in 1928 as peace trees, ten years after the peace; they are now 35 metres tall. Amersfoort's is grafted, a weeping 'Petiolaris' crown joined onto an ordinary lime rootstock, its long leaf stalks letting each leaf swivel independently in the wind.
